title: Quantile latency sentinel and synthetic workload catalog for kernel selector tuning
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Build a quantile-based latency sentinel and a reusable synthetic workload catalog ("Weft") to exercise kernel-selection heuristics, attention optimizations, and separate prefill vs. decode scheduling. Goal is deterministic CI-level regression detection and a small, representative baseline for run-to-run comparisons without relying on large production traces.

Background: Our current golden runs focus on average token throughput and single-mode synthetic traces that underrepresent skewed tail latency and mixed prefill/decode patterns (e.g., long prefill, short decode, conversatonal back-and-forth). Kernel routing changes and attention optimizations often shift the tail (p95/p99) while leaving mean unchanged. We need a compact harness that captures distributional shifts and provides actionable per-kernel signals.

Scope: 1) Implement "Weft" synthetic workload catalog with parameterized scenarios (model family, sequence-length histogram, attention sparsity patterns, KV-cache hit ratios, prefill:decode ratios, batch size distribution, token generation temperature and stop patterns). 2) Add quantile-sentinel dashboards and CI gate config (p50/p90/p95/p99, 95% CI across N runs) to the benchmark harness. 3) Instrument kernel-selection decision matrix output and expose per-kernel latencies so the selector can be traced to latency changes. 4) Integrate stable seeding, dockerized workload runners, and a lightweight variant of the golden-runbook for reproducing failures locally.

Why this differs: Instead of a single "golden baseline" we create a compact catalog of targeted scenarios (edge cases + typical patterns) that prove out kernel choices and attention optimizations. The sentinel is quantile-first (alerts on p95/p99 regressions) and includes a small randomized-run ensemble to reduce false positives from noise.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Weft catalog contains at least 12 parameterized scenarios covering: long-prefill/short-decode, conversational-turns, KV cache heavy, KV cache cold, sparse-attention patterns, micro-batch heavy, and mixed-batch latencies.
2) CI integration: a perf job runs nightly and fails when p99 latency increases >8% vs baseline on at least 2 of 3 ensemble runs or when p95 increases >10% for any scenario.
3) Benchmark harness emits per-kernel latency breakdown and kernel-selector decision logs to S3 for every run.
4) Documentation + runbook: reproducer steps, docker image tag, and troubleshooting checklist added to Confluence and linked from CI job.
5) PR with implementation + unit and e2e tests merged and non-flaky for 10 consecutive runs on CI pool.
deliverables:
- Weft synthetic workload library (python) and config YAMLs (12 scenarios)
- A quantile-sentinel module added to benchmark harness that computes per-run p50/p90/p95/p99 and ensemble CI
- CI job definition (github actions / internal runner) + failure policy
- Kernel-selector instrumentation: CSV + JSON line logs per request and aggregated per-kernel latency breakdown
- Confluence runbook and troubleshooting doc + links to sample reproducer Docker images
- Demo notebook showing how a kernel change maps to p99 delta and per-kernel attribution
approach:
Phase 1 (2 wks): design scenarios, implement synthetic generators for prefill traces and decode traces; create stable seed strategy. Phase 2 (3 wks): add quantile computation, per-kernel instrumentation, and run harness parallelization (multi-worker runners with fixed load profiles). Phase 3 (2 wks): CI integration and gating rules, noise modeling (bootstrap ensemble of N=3 runs with fixed seeds), and dashboard wiring. Phase 4 (1 wk): docs, handoff, and runbook.
Key engineering notes: decouple prefill and decode runners so prefill scheduling, KV-cache warmup, and prefetch behaviors can be toggled independently. Export kernel decisions with unique trace IDs so we can correlate kernel choices to downstream latencies. Use docker images tagged runtime-bench:weft-2026-03 for CI reproducibility.
success_metrics:
- CI false positive rate < 3% over a 30-day window (measured by manual triage).
- Detectable regressions: > 90% of deliberate kernel regressions injected in canary tests produce p99 regressions flagged by the sentinel.
- Reduced mean time-to-root-cause for kernel selection regressions from ~2 days to <8 hours (measured after rollout).
- Library adoption: at least 3 runtime-team engineers use Weft scenarios for PR-level local checks within 6 weeks.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: noisy measurements from multi-tenant CI runners causing flaky gates. Mitigation: run ensemble of 3 fixed-seed runs and require consistent signal on 2/3; add machine-type labels and only accept runs from dedicated perf runners for gating.
Risk: synthetic workload may not surface real prod edge cases. Mitigation: iterate by adding one real-production trace-derived scenario per month and keep a small pool of anonymized production-derived traces for validation.
Risk: added CI runtime cost. Mitigation: schedule heavier scenarios to nightly (not PR) and keep PR quick checks to 2-3 representative scenarios (smoke subset).
roll_out_plan:
1) Merge Weft library and sentinel to feature branch. 2) Run internal canary on dedicated perf runner for two weeks and inject synthetic regressions to validate detection. 3) Enable CI nightlies with gating but keep PR gates advisory for first 2 sprints. 4) After stability (10 consecutive non-flaky nightlies), flip PR gate to blocking for kernel routing changes. 5) Add automated triage playbook to on-call rotation.
Notes: we will tag runtime-1.22 with bench-weft-1 once merged.
